What went right: the book avoided forcing a mediocre trade for a seventh straight day, and this afternoon's risk desk correctly vetoed a UNP BUY that looked clean on the surface -- a real Q2 beat plus a real same-day Canadian National rail-access agreement supporting the pending Norfolk Southern deal. What went wrong was reasoning, not data: the vetoed proposal's own thesis stated the CN agreement was 'signed one day earlier' when every dated headline in the bundle for that story was same-session (age_days 0.2-0.6, all 2026-07-24), and it cited a favorable RBC note from the same news pull while omitting a same-pull BNSF headline publicly attacking the exact merger-approval mechanism the trade was built on -- an unforced, checkable error that the risk desk had to catch instead of the reasoning process catching it first. The one change for next week: before finalizing any BUY thesis, I will explicitly cross-check every dated or sequenced claim in the catalysts and thesis fields against the actual age_days/published timestamps of the supporting headlines in the bundle, and label the timing as unverified rather than asserting a sequence the data doesn't support -- next Friday's review grades whether that habit actually prevented a repeat of this exact failure mode.

** The bundle's price bars for a 2pm ET intraday cycle are still dated to the prior session's close (2026-07-22), so a genuinely material intraday move -- today's VIX spike and broad risk-off tape -- was only visible via an out-of-band WebSearch, not from any bundle field. A same-day intraday quote (even just SPY/VIX last + % change, refreshed per run rather than once at prior close) would let the regime read catch a live risk-off day without relying on the agent remembering to search for it.

** Two of this run's four tape/8-K promotions (S, PG) look like ticker-symbol false positives rather than real company news -- S's promoted headline is a US-China congressional statement about Ford/Geely with no SentinelOne content, and PG's is a "PG&E Q2 2026 Earnings Call" transcript (PG&E/PCG, not Procter & Gamble). A cheap fix -- requiring the company name or a word-boundary-safe ticker match in the promoted headline, not just a bare single/double-letter symbol substring -- would stop burning research slots on unrelated companies and free that promotion capacity for a real off-universe tape story.

** ANET and GE both triggered my own watchlist alerts this run but neither received the focus-tier bundle (no digest entry, no chart, no sec_filings/stack_card) that tape-promoted and mini-scan names get — I could only underwrite them off the raw universe_scan indicator row. The conclusion held (volume still neutral on both, an unambiguous read even without the deeper bundle), but a genuinely close call on either name would have been harder to underwrite properly. Trigger-alert names should get the same focus-tier promotion tape/8-K names already get.
